subject: Urgent: MedStream sustained latency breach on long-window Hosted API
messages:
From: Tom Anders <tom@medstream.ai>
To: support@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: ops@medstream.ai
Date: 2028-06-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes on hosted API for long-window completions

Hi Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained and material regression in p95/p99 latency and an uptick in 500/502 errors starting ~2028-06-02 23:00 PDT for requests that use the 32k context window. Impact: several clinical batch jobs timed out and our ingest pipeline retried aggressively which created backpressure. Sample numbers from our side (UTC): p95 ~ 1.8s -> 3.6s, p99 ~ 3.9s -> 11.2s; error rate on completions for context lengths > 24k jumped from 0.2% -> 4.6%.

We rely on your hosted API for production inference. This is high-impact for our SLAs. Can you confirm receipt and an ETA for mitigation? We can provide traces - attaching one example.

Thanks,
Tom Anders
Head of Platform, MedStream
[Attachment: medstream_traces_20280603.log (12KB)]

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 spikes on hosted API for long-window completions — triage notes

Aditya — quick triage notes from SRE:

Observations (first pass):
- Spike correlates tightly with requests where client context > 24k tokens; backlog forms on the inference front-end queues and per-model inference workers show high KV cache churn.
- Several models show GPU stalls when peak sequence lengths exceed ~26–28k tokens; memory pinning leads to occasional OOM-protect throttles and retried requests surface as 502/504 in the API layer.
- We observed a pattern of many small resume requests from a handful of API keys that cause repeated cache invalidation and kernel-selection thrashing.

Immediate containment steps we propose (can apply within 30–90 minutes):
1) Emergency policy: soft-rate-limit (>16k contexts) by 30% for hosted tier; return explicit X-Redwood-Throttle header.
2) Enable temporary route: send >28k contexts to an isolated capacity pool (cold pool) with relaxed memory oversubscription (will increase cost).
3) Deploy a hotfix for prefix/KV caching heuristics to avoid full cache eviction on resume patterns (eta ~6 hours for canary).
4) Consider a short-term customer-visible mitigation: automatic chunking for completion requests >24k (with resume tokenization) while preserving semantic correctness.

Attachments: sre_initial_summary.pdf with relevant metric graphs and sample_kv_cache_dump.txt.

I recommend we communicate these options to MedStream now and apply 1) immediately pending approval.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sre_initial_summary.pdf (180KB)]

Tom — thank you for the quick flag and for the trace. Apologies for the disruption. High-level actions we're taking right now:

1) Implementing a temporary soft-rate-limit for requests with context length > 16k to reduce queuing pressure (applies to your tenant keys) — this will be live within 60 minutes.
2) Provisioning an isolated dedicated capacity pool to accept >28k contexts from MedStream; this is a short-term routing change we can turn on for you within 4–8 hours.
3) SRE is deploying a caching heuristic patch (ETA ~6 hours) that should eliminate the repeated cache thrashing pattern.

We will keep you updated every 2 hours until stable. As a gesture, we will extend a credit for impacted usage; ops will follow up with details.

I will send a post-mitigation summary and timeline as soon as the patch is canaried. Please reply here if you prefer an immediate call — happy to jump on a bridge.

Best,

- Observed result: p99 for affected traffic returned to within 10% of baseline; error rate reduced to pre-incident levels.
- Engineering is running a post-deploy canary and working on the full root-cause postmortem (Jira INFRA-9123).

Recommendation: offer MedStream 2 months of credits on hosted usage for impacted jobs and provide white-glove migration assistance to the dedicated pool if they want to offload long-window runs. I have a postmortem draft in Drive — see link.

I'll coordinate the formal exec summary for CRO and CFO.
